business_model.basis: Stated in P1 (20-F Item 4, Business Overview)
business_model.claim: ASEH's core business is providing semiconductor packaging (assembly), testing, and interconnect materials services to semiconductor companies that outsource their manufacturing.
quotes: ASEH is a leading provider of semiconductor manufacturing services in assembly and testing.

Our services include semiconductor packaging, production of interconnect materials, front-end engineering testing, wafer probing, and final testing services, as well as integrated solutions for EMS in relation to computing, peripherals, communications, industrial, automotive, and server applications.

business_model.basis: Stated in P1 (20-F Item 4) and P2 (20-F Item 5, segment table)
business_model.claim: ASEH also generates revenue from electronic manufacturing services (EMS) through its USI Group subsidiary, covering computing, communications, industrial, and automotive applications.
quotes: USI Group engages primarily in EMS in relation to computing, consumer electronics, communications, industrial and automotive, among other services and businesses.

business_model.basis: Stated in P1 (20-F Item 4, Outsourcing Trends)
business_model.claim: ASEH's customers are primarily fabless semiconductor companies and IDMs that outsource packaging, testing, and manufacturing to independent providers.
quotes: We believe that the growth in the number and scale of fabless semiconductor companies that rely solely on independent manufacturers will continue to drive our growth.

Similarly, the availability of technologically advanced independent manufacturing services has encouraged IDMs, traditionally reliant on in-house manufacturing, to increasingly outsource their manufacturing requirements to independent semiconductor manufacturing companies.

business_model.basis: Stated in P2 (20-F Item 5, segment results table)
business_model.claim: In 2025, the three reporting segments contributed: Packaging 47.8% of operating revenues, EMS 39.9%, and Testing 11.1%.

business_model.basis: Stated in P2 (20-F Item 5, segment gross profit table)
business_model.claim: In 2025, gross margins by segment were 22.1% for Packaging, 31.0% for Testing, and 9.2% for EMS.

business_model.basis: Stated in P2 (20-F Item 5, Results of Operations, 2025 vs 2024)
business_model.claim: 2025 operating revenues grew 8.4% to NT$645,387.7 million, primarily driven by higher sales in packaging and testing, with packaging up 17.8% and testing up 31.8%.
quotes: Operating revenues increased by 8.4% to NT$645,387.7 million (US$20,573.4 million) in 2025 from NT$595,409.6 million in 2024, primarily due to higher sales in our packaging and testing business.
The increase in packaging and testing revenues was primarily driven by growing demand in our leading-edge advanced packing services and testing business.

business_model.basis: Stated in P2 (20-F Item 5, cost breakdown table and narrative)
business_model.claim: In 2025, raw material costs were 48.4% of operating revenues, labor 11.3%, and depreciation, amortization and rental 9.6%, for a total operating cost ratio of 82.3%.
quotes: In 2024 and 2025, raw material cost as a percentage of our operating revenues was 51.5% and 48.4%, respectively.
Raw materials | 53.3% | 51.5% | 48.4%
Depreciation, amortization and rental expense | 9.0% | 9.1% | 9.6%
Total operating costs | 84.2% | 83.7% | 82.3%

business_model.basis: Stated in P2 (20-F Item 5, Pricing and Revenue Mix)
business_model.claim: The majority of ASEH's prices and revenues are denominated in U.S. dollars, and the silicon die is typically supplied by customers on a consignment basis so its cost is not reflected in ASEH's revenues.
quotes: The majority of our prices and revenues is denominated in U.S. dollars.

In the case of semiconductor packaging, the cost of the silicon die, typically the most costly component of the packaged semiconductor, is usually not reflected in our costs (or revenues) since it is generally supplied by our customers on a consignment basis.

business_model.basis: Stated in P2 (20-F Item 5, High Fixed Costs)
business_model.claim: ASEH's operations, particularly testing, are characterized by relatively high fixed costs, and profitability is sensitive to capacity utilization rates.
quotes: Our operations, in particular our testing operations, are characterized by relatively high fixed costs.

Increases or decreases in our capacity utilization rates could have a significant effect on gross margins since the unit cost of our products and/or services generally decreases as fixed costs are allocated over a larger number of units.

P2.s168.text: Our gross profit as a percentage of operating revenues, or gross margin, was 17.7% in 2025 compared to 16.3% in 2024, which was primarily as a result of higher packaging and testing revenue mix and higher factory utilization of our packaging and testing equipment, offset in part by the appreciating NT dollars and higher utility costs.

P2.s175.text: As a percentage of operating revenues, depreciation, amortization, and rental expenses increased to 9.6% in 2025 from 9.1% in 2024, primarily attributed to continuing investment in production capacity for advanced technologies.

P6.s28.text: Fourth Quarter 2026 Outlook (1/2) Based on our current business outlook and exchange rate assumptions of 1 US dollar to 31 .9 NT dollars (versus 31 .9 in 3 rd quarter 2026) , management projects overall performance for the fourth quarter of 2026 to be as follows:  Consolidated  In NT dollar terms, our consolidated 4th quarter revenue should grow by 6 to 8 percent quarter over quarter;  Our consolidated 4th quarter gross margin should be between 23% to 24%;  Our consolidated 4th quarter operating margin should be between 14.5% to 15.5%.
